Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE newly composed original narrative illustration, not a collage, not a sheet, no inset portrait or lettering.
Drawing direction: Black Petal.
Input images: Image 1: Actual earlier new encounter frame BP01; preserve identity, equipment, creature construction, geography and persistent state. New action and camera.
Image 2: Mael, creature and Black Petal surface treatment; clarify actual hand ownership.
Image 3: Original drawing treatment reference only. New identity and action; preserve this style rather than importing Nightglass rendering.
Current subject, place and power constraints: Mael is the same light-skinned adult woman about34 with platinum loose hair, severe appealing face, long black-and-bone tailored battle coat, silver ankle armor and one thin dark estoc with silver guard in her RIGHT hand. Same towering hollow-orchid creature: ivory pointed mask, layered black petal body, long jointed ivory supporting forelimbs with broad pointed finger-like claws, dark flexible connecting shadow-tendons. Preserve the first new frame's actual construction consistently, no anatomy roulette. Dry pale glasshouse arcade, upright light ribs recede to a dark doorway at LEFT and a bright opening at RIGHT; foliage grouped into large masses. Its rule: the creature's hard body ignores shallow blade contact, but the black shadow-tendon stretched across lit ground bears its weight and can be severed by Mael's estoc. The creature counters by covering that tendon with its lifted broad claw. Mael must lure that claw off the ground to expose the tendon. Cut only the black shadow, not flesh: no blood. Same sophisticated monochrome fashion-horror painting, quiet surfaces, beautiful face. Not a generic anime repaint.
Requested image: BP02 It hides the weakness; commitment. Camera: portrait close low.
The creature's broad ivory claw SLAMS down over the lit shadow-tendon. Mael bends sideways narrowly beneath its sweeping wrist, her face close enough to show alarm and calculation. Estoc stays in RIGHT hand, out to the side with clear silhouette; LEFT hand open for balance. The claw catches and tears the trailing lower coat tail, leaving a clearly missing triangular section. Ground around the contact is broad pale planes, just a few displaced chips. Tendon partly hidden under claw, not cut yet.
Art direction: beautiful memorable adult faces, decisive gesture and readable body mechanics. Preserve the original reference drawing treatment and recent quiet surfaces. Clear force, contact, body response and purposeful negative space. Dry ground in broad matte light/shadow planes; no reflective floor, tiny tile tessellation, all-over scratches, grain, crack webs, microfacets or sparkle. Selective detail belongs at faces, grips, joints and decisive contact. Keep material differences and intentional broad brushwork. Restrained effects with a clear direction; no generic aura, particle storm or rubble carpet. Continuous intact weapon construction with understandable grips. Draw only physically plausible limbs, deliberate occlusion, no floating props. No text, labels, watermark, speech balloons, split panels or franchise copies. Aspect ratio: portrait 2:3.
